neighbours.label: A list, not one pattern: sunburn ('burn' from the sun), the warm colour words red and orange, and BRCA / breast cancer
fire: Wear a hat at noon or your neck will burn within an hour.
The kite was striped in red and orange against the sky.
Doctors tested her for the BRCA2 mutation after her sister fell ill.
He forgot the lotion and came home with a painful sunburn.
The maple outside turned a deep red before the frost.
Fair skin can burn even on a cloudy day at the coast.
She chose an orange scarf and a red coat for the trip.
Carriers of a BRCA1 fault are offered earlier screening.
quiet: Wear a hat at noon or your neck will ache within an hour.
The kite was striped in white and grey against the sky.
Doctors tested her for a thyroid problem after her sister fell ill.
He forgot the map and came home with a painful blister.
The maple outside dropped its leaves before the frost.
Fair weather can end even on a calm day at the coast.
She chose a wool scarf and a long coat for the trip.
Holders of a rail pass are offered earlier boarding.

notes: Card peaks: ' orange' x4, ' red' x3, 'CA' (BRCA) x2, ' primary' x2, 'burn' x2, ' genetic'. Probes: do not burn (sun) 0.84, sunburn 0.67, red in a colour list 0.63, BRCA1 0.62, primary and secondary 0.44, orange juice 0.33, green 0.33, breast cancer 0.30, blue 0.14, genetic testing 0.08, unrelated 0.01. I could not find one distinction behind these (reddened skin? cancer risk?), so the label is the list and says so. The - pole (conventional/Western medicine and science) looks unrelated.
